summary: Dorji Wangchuk is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, later becoming a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2009.

Dorothy C. Wong works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She is a faculty member at the University of Virginia and was a visiting professor at the University of Hong Kong's Centre of Buddhist Studies (attested 2009).

Douglas Allen is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Yale, Banaras Hindu University, and Vanderbilt, before teaching at Southern Illinois, Central Connecticut, and the University of Maine, where he became Professor Emeritus in 2020.

Douglas Fairchild Ober specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Washington and completed his PhD at the University of British Columbia under Harjot Oberoi (attested 2016).
Douglas Gildow is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Princeton University (attested 2016) under the supervision of Stephen F. Teiser and Qi Zhou.

Douglas Osto specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a Master's at the University of Washington and a PhD from SOAS under Ulrich Pagel, becoming Senior Lecturer and Programme Coordinator at Massey University in 2005.

Douglas S. Duckworth is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied at James Madison University and earned his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins, later teaching at East Tennessee State University (~2007-2013).
Dragana Majhen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned a Master's degree at the University of Manitoba under the supervision of Albert Welter (attested 2010).

Dragomir Dimitrov specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn and held posts at Marburg (attested 2002, 2017-2020) and the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project.

Dramdul is a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004-2012) and editor-in-chief for Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013-2020).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Ayu Khandro, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
Drolma is a Tibetology scholar who studied for an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and taught numerous students, including Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche and Keith Dowman.

Dudjom Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Mindrolling, Dorje Drak, Tarje Tingpoling, and Kathok monasteries under teachers including Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught figures like Gyurme Dorje.

Duncan Ryūken Williams is a Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology scholar. He studied at Reed College and Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi, and later held posts at UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
